cues.en: Instructor: There are quite a few different correlation measures.
cues.zh: 講師：相關指標有相當多種。

cues.en: To be honest, I'm not sure how many different correlations exist in total in human civilization.
cues.zh: 老實說，我不確定整個人類文明到底發明了幾種相關。

cues.en: But certainly the three most commonly used are Pearson, that's by far the most commonly used correlation measure.
cues.zh: 但最常用的三種，首先肯定是皮爾森，它的使用頻率遙遙領先。

cues.en: Spearman, which is probably the next most commonly used.
cues.zh: 其次是史皮爾曼，大概是第二常用。

cues.en: And then Ken Dell's correlation, which is what I'm going to introduce you to in this video and then the next video in code.
cues.zh: 再來是肯德爾相關，這支影片會介紹，下一支則用程式碼示範。

cues.en: So Kendell correlation is a very specific type of correlation.
cues.zh: 肯德爾相關是非常特定的一種相關。

cues.en: This is not something you would generally use.
cues.zh: 一般情況不會使用。

cues.en: You only use it when you have ordinal data.
cues.zh: 只有序位資料才會用到。

cues.en: So remember, ordinal data is data that are categorical, so they're not intrinsically numeric.
cues.zh: 記住，序位資料屬於類別資料，本質上不是數值。

cues.en: You can assign numbers to ordinal data.
cues.zh: 可以替序位資料指定數字。

cues.en: So there is an ordering, there's a natural ordering, but there's no fixed relationship across the different levels.
cues.zh: 它有順序、有自然排序，但不同層級之間沒有固定關係。

cues.en: So let me give you some examples.
cues.zh: 舉幾個例子。

cues.en: Education.
cues.zh: 教育程度。

cues.en: So if you think of middle school, high school, bachelor's degree, master's, and PhD degree, those are categories.
cues.zh: 例如國中、高中、學士、碩士與博士，這些都是類別。

cues.en: They have a meaningful relationship, but there's not necessarily a intrinsically meaningful fixed numerical relationship across them.
cues.zh: 它們之間有有意義的關係，但不一定存在本質上有意義、固定的數值關係。

cues.en: So the difference between middle school and high school is not the same as the difference between a master's degree and a PhD degree.
cues.zh: 國中到高中的差異，與碩士到博士的差異不同。

cues.en: And then another example, which is now the ubiquitous in modern human civilization is all these ratings.
cues.zh: 另一個在現代人類文明中無所不在的例子，就是各種評分。

cues.en: So you think of movie ratings, book ratings, you know, you buy a some toilet paper on Amazon and you get asked to rate the toilet paper.
cues.zh: 例如電影、書籍評分，甚至在 Amazon 買衛生紙，也會被要求替衛生紙評分。

cues.en: I don't even know why that's...
cues.zh: 我甚至不知道這是為了什麼……

cues.en: Anyway.
cues.zh: 總之。

cues.en: And of course, this course, you know, you're gonna be asked to review this course.
cues.zh: 當然，這門課也會請你評價。

cues.en: I hope you're more up here than down here.
cues.zh: 希望你的評分比較靠這邊，而不是那邊。

cues.en: But you know, give your honest opinion.
cues.zh: 不過，請提供誠實的意見。

cues.en: But anyway, these are not numerical data.
cues.zh: 總之，這些不是數值資料。

cues.en: We can assign numbers to them.
cues.zh: 可以替它們指定數字。

cues.en: So we say this is one star, two star, and so on to five stars.
cues.zh: 例如一顆星、兩顆星，一直到五顆星。

cues.en: But these are not really numeric data.
cues.zh: 但這些其實不是數值資料。

cues.en: And there's a couple of ways to justify that or to understand why that is the case.
cues.zh: 有幾種方式可以說明，或理解為什麼如此。

cues.en: For one thing, the difference between one star and two stars is not the same thing as the difference between four stars and five stars.
cues.zh: 首先，一顆星與兩顆星的差異，和四顆星與五顆星的差異不同。

cues.en: Furthermore, you cannot just sum across these stars.
cues.zh: 另外，也不能直接把星星相加。

cues.en: So you know, if we have five students who hated this course, they gave it a one star, that's really awful.
cues.zh: 假設有五位學生討厭這門課，各給一顆星，那真的很糟。

cues.en: I mean, if you really don't like this course that much, please tell me.
cues.zh: 如果你真的那麼不喜歡這門課，請告訴我。

cues.en: And then maybe there's some way I can improve it.
cues.zh: 或許我能想辦法改進。

cues.en: But anyway, five students who hated this course, they each give it one star rating.
cues.zh: 總之，五位討厭這門課的學生，各給一顆星。

cues.en: Now, I cannot combine all five of those ratings and turn that into one five star rating.
cues.zh: 我不能把五個評分加起來，變成一個五星評分。

cues.en: I mean, it would be cool if I could do that, but that doesn't even make sense.
cues.zh: 如果可以當然很好，但根本不合理。

cues.en: I mean, when I explain it out loud, it's not even a sensible thing.
cues.zh: 光是說出來，就知道不合理。

cues.en: You can't take a one star rating and a two star rating and say, well, those two together are equivalent to a three star rating.
cues.zh: 不能把一星與二星評分加在一起，說它們等同於一個三星評分。

cues.en: Okay, so these are ordinal data.
cues.zh: 這些就是序位資料。

cues.en: We can assign numbers to them.
cues.zh: 可以指定數字。

cues.en: There is an intrinsic ordering, but there's no fixed relationship across the levels.
cues.zh: 有內在順序，但不同層級之間沒有固定關係。

cues.en: We can't really treat these as if they are numbers like on an interval or ratio scale or even discreet scale.
cues.zh: 不能把它們當成等距或等比尺度，甚至離散尺度上的數字來處理。

cues.en: So when you have data like this and you want to correlate that with some other kind of data, then the Kendall correlation is the right analysis approach to take.
cues.zh: 因此，當你有這種資料，又想與其他資料計算相關，肯德爾相關就是合適的分析方法。

cues.en: Now, in theory, you can apply a Pearson correlation.
cues.zh: 理論上，當然也能套用皮爾森相關。

cues.en: That's like technically possible.
cues.zh: 技術上可行。

cues.en: You can go through the math, you can call the code.
cues.zh: 可以進行數學運算，也可以呼叫程式碼。

cues.en: And in a few videos from now there's gonna be an unsupervised learning project.
cues.zh: 再過幾支影片，會有一個無監督學習專案。

cues.en: And also in the next video, in the next code video, you'll see some comparisons.
cues.zh: 下一支程式影片也會做一些比較。

cues.en: And it's interesting to see whether the Pearson correlation is actually bad to implement for these kinds of data, or if it's pretty robust and it doesn't make such a big deal either way.
cues.zh: 看看皮爾森相關用於這些資料，是否真的不好，還是其實很穩健，用哪一種都差不多，會很有意思。

cues.en: Okay, but nonetheless, this is the point of Kendall's correlation.
cues.zh: 總之，這就是肯德爾相關的用意。

cues.en: It's only for correlation with ordinal data.
cues.zh: 只用於涉及序位資料的相關。

cues.en: Okay, so I'm gonna explain briefly how it works.
cues.zh: 接著簡單解釋運作方式。

cues.en: The main idea is to transform the data into rank concordances and concordances here.
cues.zh: 主要概念是把資料轉換成秩的一致性，這裡的一致性，

cues.en: Well, the word concordance means agreement between two different things.
cues.zh: 就是指兩個不同東西彼此相符。

cues.en: And rank concordances means relative signs, this is how it gets operationalized.
cues.zh: 秩的一致性，在操作上透過相對符號來定義。

cues.en: Relative signs across the values per variable.
cues.zh: 也就是每個變數內，各數值之間的相對符號。

cues.en: So in the next slide, I'm going to give you an overview of the formula.
cues.zh: 下一張投影片會概述公式。

cues.en: I'm not gonna go into too much detail about all the nitty gritty aspects, but I will give you a bit of a sense of how the formula works.
cues.zh: 不會深入所有細節，但會讓你稍微了解公式如何運作。

cues.en: And then there's something else you should know that there's a little extension to the Kendall correlation.
cues.zh: 另外還要知道，肯德爾相關有一個小擴充。

cues.en: It's called Kendall tau-b.
cues.zh: 稱為肯德爾 tau-b。

cues.en: So essentially there's two versions of the Kendall correlation.
cues.zh: 基本上，肯德爾相關有兩個版本。

cues.en: One is called tau-a, and one is called tau-b.
cues.zh: 一個是 tau-a，一個是 tau-b。

cues.en: And tau-b includes an adjustment for ties, and that's the one that's really often used.
cues.zh: tau-b 包含對同秩的調整，也是很常使用的版本。

cues.en: Tau-a just has a simplified normalization factor.
cues.zh: tau-a 的正規化因子比較簡單。

cues.en: So it can actually underestimate the true correlation in the data.
cues.zh: 因此，它可能低估資料中的真正相關。

cues.en: Okay, once you compute the Kendall tau, it's often called tau instead of R, like with Pearson and Spearman.
cues.zh: 算出肯德爾 tau 之後——它常稱為 tau，而不是皮爾森與史皮爾曼使用的 r——

cues.en: Then the interpretation of the Kendall correlation coefficient is identical to the interpretation of the Spearman and the Pearson correlation.
cues.zh: 其相關係數的解讀，與史皮爾曼和皮爾森相關完全相同。

cues.en: So Kendall tau is bound between minus one and plus one, minus one means perfectly negatively correlated.
cues.zh: 肯德爾 tau 介於負 1 到正 1，負 1 表示完全負相關。

cues.en: Zero means not at all correlated.
cues.zh: 0 表示完全不相關。

cues.en: The two variables are totally unrelated to each other, and one means that the two variables are perfectly correlated.
cues.zh: 兩個變數彼此完全無關，而 1 表示兩者完全相關。

cues.en: And also all the other things you've learned about correlations over this section also apply to Kendall as well.
cues.zh: 本單元學到的其他相關概念，也都適用於肯德爾相關。

cues.en: So for example, if you have a modest correlation, it might be non-significant, not statistically significant with a small n.
cues.zh: 例如，中等程度的相關在 N 很小時，可能不顯著，也就是未達統計顯著。

cues.en: And if you add more and more data, the P value is gonna get smaller and smaller.
cues.zh: 隨著資料愈來愈多，P 值會愈來愈小。

cues.en: So all the things that you have learned to interpret about Pearson and Spearman also apply to the Kendall tau.
cues.zh: 因此，學過的皮爾森與史皮爾曼的解讀方式，也適用於肯德爾 tau。

cues.en: So here we see the formula.
cues.zh: 這裡是公式。

cues.en: So we have a sum here.
cues.zh: 這裡有一個總和。

cues.en: This is the signum or the sign function.
cues.zh: 這是 signum，也就是 sign 符號函式。

cues.en: So that's just returning a minus one for any negative numbers, zero for zero, and plus one for any positive numbers.
cues.zh: 負數回傳負 1，0 回傳 0，正數回傳正 1。

cues.en: And the x and the y are the two variables.
cues.zh: X 與 Y 是兩個變數。

cues.en: And the tilde on top is for the rank version of x.
cues.zh: 上方的波浪號表示 X 的秩版本。

cues.en: Tilde is for indicating rank is non-standard.
cues.zh: 用波浪號表示秩，並不是標準用法。

cues.en: I don't know if you'll see it in other books or courses, but this is what I've been trying to use consistently in this course.
cues.zh: 我不知道其他書或課程會不會這樣用，但這是我在本課程盡量一致採用的符號。

cues.en: Okay, so we have tilde as the ranks, and then the Ith rank, we're summing over from I to N.
cues.zh: 波浪號表示秩，接著是第 i 個秩，從 i 到 N 加總。

cues.en: And I'm abusing the notation a little bit here.
cues.zh: 這裡的符號用得有一點不嚴謹。

cues.en: It's kind of a mix of math notation and python notation.
cues.zh: 有點混合了數學符號與 Python 寫法。

cues.en: So essentially what's going on here, what this formula says is that we compute the ranks of the variables, and then we compute the signs
cues.zh: 基本上，公式表示先計算變數的秩，再計算每個元素 i 相對於

cues.en: of the each individual element I relative to the rest of the points in the data.
cues.zh: 資料中其他點的符號。

cues.en: So this would be from index I up until the end of the variable, the end of the data vector X.
cues.zh: 也就是從索引 i 一直到變數末端，也就是資料向量 X 的末端。

cues.en: And same thing for Y.
cues.zh: Y 也一樣。

cues.en: So the idea of this product inside this summation is that we want to know if x is relatively large or small
cues.zh: 總和裡面這個乘積的概念，是要知道 X 相對而言較大還是較小，

cues.en: compared to the rest of x.
cues.zh: 與其餘 X 相比。

cues.en: And if y, the Ith element in y is relatively larger or smaller compared to the other rank transformed elements in y.
cues.zh: 以及 Y 的第 i 個元素，相較於 Y 中其他秩轉換後的元素，是較大還是較小。

cues.en: Now we can think about what's going to happen when the values and x are relatively small, so small relative to the other values and x.
cues.zh: 想想，X 的值相對較小，也就是小於 X 中其他數值時，會如何。

cues.en: And when y is also relatively small, relative to x.
cues.zh: 而 Y 也相對較小，相對於 X。

cues.en: And we're gonna have, the sign is gonna be minus times minus, which is gonna give us plus.
cues.zh: 符號就會是負乘負，得到正。

cues.en: And conversely, if xi is relatively large compared to the rest of x, and if yi is relatively large compared to the rest of x, then we get a plus sign here and a plus sign here.
cues.zh: 反過來，如果 Xᵢ 相較其餘 X 較大，而 Yᵢ 相較其餘 X 也較大，這裡得到正號，這裡也得到正號。

cues.en: So you can see these are concordances.
cues.zh: 所以你可以看到，這些就是一致性。

cues.en: When the x's and the y's are relatively low or relatively high compared to their own ranked distribution, then we end up with a lot of positive number,
cues.zh: 當 X 與 Y 相對於各自的秩分布，都比較低或都比較高，最後就會得到很多正數，

cues.en: plus signs here, plus ones.
cues.zh: 這裡很多正號、正 1。

cues.en: So this thing grows, this gets large and positive.
cues.zh: 所以這一項會增加，變成很大的正值。

cues.en: And when the x's are relatively high and the y's are relatively low, we're gonna have plus signs times minus signs, and that's going to give us small negative numbers,
cues.zh: 當 X 相對較高，而 Y 相對較低時，就會有正號乘負號，得到小的負數，

cues.en: which will decrease this overall.
cues.zh: 讓整體數值降低。

cues.en: Now, the result of this sum is not bound by one.
cues.zh: 這個總和的結果不受 1 限制。

cues.en: So this is going to be, the result of this sum is going to be some integer value, and it can be, you know, sort of arbitrarily large, depending on how long the data vectors are.
cues.zh: 總和會得到某個整數，依資料向量長度而定，可能任意大。

cues.en: So that's why we have this normalization factor K.
cues.zh: 所以需要這個正規化因子 K。

cues.en: So this goes in the denominator, it's K to the minus one power.
cues.zh: 它放在分母，也就是 K 的負 1 次方。

cues.en: And I'm not going to define K because this is where the correlation starts getting particularly hairy, especially for the tau-b version.
cues.zh: 我不會定義 K，因為這部分的相關計算開始變得很複雜，尤其是 tau-b 版本。

cues.en: But basically, K is designed to be the maximum possible value that this thing could be if there were 100% concordances.
cues.zh: 基本上，K 被設計成這一項在 100% 一致時，可能達到的最大值。

cues.en: So that scales it down to one.
cues.zh: 如此就能把它縮放到 1。

cues.en: Now the thing is that it's not simply the number of pairs that we have in x and y because we also have to account for the ties if there are any ties
cues.zh: 但它不只是 X 與 Y 的配對數量，因為秩轉換時，如果有同秩，

cues.en: when we rank transform the data.
cues.zh: 還必須把同秩納入考量。

cues.en: So K is actually not just the number of total possible comparisons, but it also gets this adjustment for the number of ties.
cues.zh: 因此，K 並非只有所有可能比較的總數，還會根據同秩數量調整。

cues.en: Anyway, if you're really curious, if you really wanna nerd out on Saturday nights, then go for it and look up the full formula for the Kendall tau-b correlation.
cues.zh: 如果真的好奇，想在週六晚上好好鑽研，就去查肯德爾 tau-b 相關的完整公式。

cues.en: But I hope that this is sufficient amount of knowledge for you to get some insight into how this analysis works.
cues.zh: 不過，希望這些知識已足夠讓你了解這個分析如何運作。

cues.en: Okay, so in this video, I introduced you to the Kendall correlation.
cues.zh: 這支影片介紹了肯德爾相關。

cues.en: And again, the Kendall correlation is very specific.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，肯德爾相關用途很特定。

cues.en: It's only for ordinal data.
cues.zh: 只用於序位資料。
